export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to goods exported outside the EU and services supplied to non-EU clients where performance occurs outside France; requires proof of non-residency and service delivery

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent zero-rating claims attract penalties up to 80% of evaded VAT plus interest; retrospective clawback with potential criminal tax evasion proceedings

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) as the national central bank within the Eurosystem, with the European Central Bank (ECB) exercising exclusive competence over euro monetary policy and foreign-exchange reserve operations for the euro area. Exchange-control supervision and balance-of-payments statistical administration are carried out by the Banque de France under Articles L151-1 to L165-1 of the Code monétaire et financier (Monetary and Financial Code), while EU/UN sanctions screening and asset-freeze administration are coordinated with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for both current-account and capital-account transactions. France honours IMF Article VIII obligations and applies the EU capital-movement framework (TFEU Articles 63-66), which permits unrestricted dividend distributions, profit repatriation, intercompany loans, equity capital contributions, and liquidation proceeds without prior central-bank authorization. The only operative gates are (i) balance-of-payments statistical declaration to the Banque de France for cross-border flows above the regulatory reporting thresholds, including the direct-investment declaration duty for transactions exceeding EUR 75,000; (ii) annual foreign-asset reporting on French tax form 3916 for any bank account held outside France; and (iii) EU/UN/OFAC financial sanctions screening enforced by the French banking system. Capital-account restrictions are limited to prior approval for foreign direct investment in sensitive defence, public-security, and critical-technology sectors under Article R151-3 of the FDI decree, which does not apply to an ISIC 7810 student-placement and visa-advisory operation. Profit remittance hurdles are purely tax-driven: dividends to non-resident shareholders are subject to 25% withholding tax, reducible under applicable double tax treaties, with no foreign-exchange limitation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender obligation exists under French law. Export receipts, including service fees collected from non-resident international students and partner agencies, may be retained indefinitely in EUR or any foreign currency in French or foreign bank accounts; there is no mandatory conversion ratio and no statutory timeline for repatriation. The only compliance duties are (i) accurate bookkeeping and VAT treatment of zero-rated service exports, (ii) disclosure of any foreign-held bank accounts on annual tax form 3916, and (iii) balance-of-payments statistical reporting for cross-border flows, handled by the French relationship bank as resident reporting intermediary.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for operational treasury purposes; Low for regulated escrow custody. French-licensed Electronic Money Institutions such as Qonto, Shine, and Treezor can open a corporate IBAN rapidly, provide payment cards, invoicing tools, and FX conversion; however, an EMI is not a credit institution, cannot hold client monies in a legal 'séquestre' escrow, cannot grant credit, and must safeguard funds through a partner credit institution. Offshore non-EEA EMIs, including UK and US digital banks, are effectively non-viable as primary treasury rails because the PSD2 passport regime requires an EEA authorisation; a non-EEA EMI would need a French-licensed branch or agent to operate lawfully. Given the Medium_Risk_Enhanced classification of the immigration/visa advisory business, the primary operating account must remain at a French credit institution, with the EMI channel restricted to day-to-day expense payments.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of the SAS President, or at least one statutory director, together with the principal ultimate beneficial owner, is the prevailing market standard for Tier-1 French banks when the client risk tier is Medium_Risk_Enhanced. Articles L561-5 to L561-13 and R561-5 of the Code monétaire et financier do not formally impose an in-person interview, and remote onboarding with eIDAS-qualified electronic signature plus video identification is accepted by some digital-first banks; however, all major French credit institutions in practice require at least one physical or interactive videoconference identification step with the Président. The documentary package must include a K-bis extract issued within three months, certified articles of association, proof of registered office, identity documents and proof of address for all shareholders holding more than 25%, and the beneficial-owner declaration. Remote opening is possible only through fintech banks and still requires a notarised or apostilled corporate bundle and signed statutory declarations on beneficial ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity or nominee-shareholder pattern in the SAS capital structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the articles of association (statuts), K-bis extract issued within three months, shareholder register, beneficial-owner declaration (Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs, INF 2257) filed and stamped by the French Commercial Court (Greffe), identity documents and proof of residential address for every shareholder holding 25% or more, and a written explanation of the shareholding purpose. If the parent is a foreign education group, provide the consolidated group structure chart and notarised or apostilled corporate documents of the parent entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or PEP filter hits caused by student applicants, partner agencies, or remitters domiciled in OFAC/EU-sanctioned or embargoed jurisdictions (e.g., Russia, Belarus, Iran, Syria) or by politically exposed persons.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written sanctions-compliance policy and risk-appetite statement, client risk-rating matrix, enhanced due diligence file per applicant (passport copy, visa application, university offer letter), documentary proof that the SAS acts only as an advisory intermediary and does not route funds to sanctioned parties, and a documented 'benign match' decision issued by the SAS compliance officer for each screening hit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Aggregated cross-border receipt and disbursement structure resembling alternative remittance or tuition-fee pass-through, with mixing of client fees and earned advisory fees in the same account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed engagement letters and fee schedules, segregated accounting framework isolating disbursed third-party costs (university tuition, health insurance, housing deposits) from earned advisory fees, monthly reconciliation reports, underlying invoices from universities, insurers, and landlords, and a signed commitment to operate a client-money ledger or a bank-hosted compte séquestre for any monies held on behalf of clients.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained source of wealth or source of funds for the initial capital injection and subsequent shareholder loans in the immigration and golden-visa advisory business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank reference letters from the shareholder's home bank dated within three months, gift or debt confirmation agreements, board resolution of the SAS approving the capital injection, corporate tax registration documents of the shareholder, and source-of-wealth documentation comprising the last two years of audited accounts or tax returns, sale or purchase deeds for any funded asset dispositions, and evidence of salary or bonus income.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol for the non-resident shareholder capital injection: (1) the shareholder wires via SWIFT MT103 to the SAS euro IBAN at the French relationship bank; (2) the payment instruction must be coded with the French interbank balance-of-payments motif as 'Apport en capital (direct investment)' and the purpose description 'Capital Contribution – SAS statutory share capital and share premium'; (3) the French bank, acting as resident reporting intermediary, records the transaction under the Banque de France balance-of-payments regime when the flow exceeds EUR 75,000 and screens the remitter against EU, UN, and OFAC sanctions and PEP registries; (4) the SAS must evidence receipt with the shareholder subscription resolution and the bank attestation de dépôt des fonds submitted to the Greffe to complete the capital formation; (5) for non-EU shareholders, provide apostilled corporate authorisations, and complete the bank's FATCA and CRS tax self-certification forms. A euro-denominated injection is recommended to eliminate FX settlement risk; non-euro injections require the bank's FX conversion ticket and remain subject to the same balance-of-payments declaration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements to host universities, foreign language schools, insurance providers, and overseas partner agencies are cleared using: (a) SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) for euro payments to EU/EEA beneficiaries, with the beneficiary IBAN, BIC, and a remittance caption referencing the student file; (b) SWIFT MT103 for non-euro and extra-EEA payments, notably USD, GBP, and CNY flows to tuition-fee lockboxes or agency commissions, including the balance-of-payments purpose code and supporting invoice; and (c) Commercial Letters of Credit governed by UCP600 where a large prepayment or milestone payment is secured by enrolment contracts and proforma invoices, issuable through all Tier-1 relationship banks although rarely cost-effective for small consultative fees. Every outbound wire must be matched against the AML/CFT business model and, when disbursing from a client-money ledger, must be pre-authorised in the underlying escrow agreement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forwards (change à terme) with EEA-licensed credit institutions for maturities up to 12 months, documented under a local ISDA or European Master Agreement or the bank's standard treasury terms, hedging EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and EUR/CNH mismatches between tuition receivables and partner payables

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing restricted or non-convertible currencies such as CNH, INR, KRW, and BRL, used solely to hedge bona fide student-fee flows without physical settlement, subject to MiFID II professional-client classification and the bank's global-markets margin documentation

Cross-currency swaps (swaps de change) for longer-dated synthetic conversion of non-euro financing or multi-year placement contracts, executed bilaterally with a French Tier-1 counterparty and subject to EMIR reporting plus initial-margin and variation-margin rules where clearing thresholds apply
Spot FX conversion (change au comptant) as the default de minimis hedging tool for operational currency conversions executed through the bank's electronic FX platform

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval and filing of annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry (Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce) through the INPI formalities portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval within six months after financial year-end; filing within one month after approval, or within two months if filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court order to file, possible daily coercive penalty, civil fine generally up to EUR 1,500 and up to EUR 3,000 for repeat non-compliance; persistent inactivity may lead to administrative removal from the RCS after notice procedures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (Form 2065 and financial schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration (Direction générale des finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after financial year-end, or by the second business day following 1 May for a calendar-year company, subject to the applicable electronic filing timetable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing interest and tax surcharge, generally 10% for failure or delay without an approved extension; higher penalties may apply for deliberate or repeated non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts approval and corporate decision records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Maintained in the company's statutory records; filing consequences are handled by the Commercial Court Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval within six months after financial year-end, with minutes and resolutions retained with the corporate records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to document or approve accounts may expose the legal representative to liability, court-ordered compliance, and related late-filing sanctions

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally mandatory when the SAS exceeds at least two of the following thresholds at the relevant statutory test date: EUR 5 million balance-sheet total, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Separate mandatory-audit rules may apply to certain groups and controlled entities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the French Accounting Standards Authority (ANC) regulations for statutory accounts. IFRS may apply to qualifying consolidated accounts or where legally permitted, but does not generally replace French GAAP for individual statutory accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not require a standalone annual UBO confirmation solely because a new year begins. The SAS must identify and report beneficial owners and update the beneficial-owner filing promptly, generally within 30 days of a change in ownership, control, or identifying information. Share transfers must be documented in the company's share-transfer and shareholder records and reflected in the UBO filing where control changes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of shareholders or share accounts and share-transfer records
Minute book or electronic record of shareholder and corporate decisions
Beneficial-owner register and supporting ownership-control documentation
Accounting books and annual financial statements

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 300-1,200 per year, approximately USD 325-1,300; France has no general annual franchise-tax renewal fee for an SAS
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 3,000-12,000 per year, approximately USD 3,250-13,000 for a small or medium-sized SAS, depending on turnover, group structure, and accounting complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% corporate income tax on taxable profits. A qualifying small enterprise may access a 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of profit, generally subject to annual turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million, fully paid-up share capital, and at least 75% ownership by individuals or qualifying entities.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The 15% small-enterprise rate applies only within its statutory conditions and profit ceiling. France also permits research and development tax credits, apprenticeship and training-related credits, and other sector-specific credits where conditions are satisfied. Loss utilization is restricted by an annual cap generally equal to EUR 1 million plus 50% of the portion of current-year taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. France generally permits unused tax losses to be carried forward without a fixed expiry period, subject to statutory limitations and continuity-of-business rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD, Corporate Income Tax Return, together with the relevant annexes, including Forms 2058-A-SD through 2058-C-SD and tax-accounting schedules 2050-SD through 2057-SD, filed electronically through the French tax administration's EDI-TDFC channel or EFI service on the impots.gouv.fr professional portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual for the corporate income tax return. Corporate income tax instalments are generally paid quarterly, with a final balancing payment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a financial year ending on 31 December, the return is generally due by the second business day after 1 May of the following year. For a financial year ending on a date other than 31 December, the return is generally due within three months after the year-end. The final corporate income tax balance is generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month following year-end, subject to the statutory calendar applicable to the taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered office, SIREN number, principal activity, financial year dates, tax office, and filing status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the French SAS legal name and SIREN exactly as registered. Disclose the French registered office and identify the foreign shareholder or parent in the ownership and related-party information where required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable result determined from accounting profit or loss after French tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only the French SAS's taxable result. Do not include the foreign shareholder's or parent company's separate profits unless a valid French tax consolidation regime applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting result to taxable result, including nondeductible expenses, exempt income, depreciation adjustments, provisions, and other permanent or temporary differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disallow shareholder distributions, unsupported management charges, non-arm's-length expenses, penalties, and expenses lacking a French business purpose. Apply withholding tax, treaty, and permanent-establishment analysis separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses carried forward and losses used in the current period, subject to the annual utilization cap.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document the origin, amount, and continuity of French tax losses. A change in activity, cessation, merger, or material restructuring may restrict or eliminate loss utilization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and other offsets available against corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only credits supported by statutory records, including eligible research and development or employment-related expenditure. Foreign tax credits are generally treaty- or statute-dependent and must not be claimed without supporting documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Forms 2050-SD to 2057-SD, accounting balance sheet and income statement
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assets, liabilities, income, expenses, depreciation, provisions, and financial statement data.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile reported figures to French statutory accounts and the general ledger. Related-party balances, shareholder loans, intercompany receivables, and foreign-currency items must be separately supportable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2065-SD, related-party and tax group information
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information concerning tax consolidation, related entities, ownership, and specific tax elections where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify foreign controlling entities, permanent establishments, tax group membership, and material related-party transactions. Verify whether the SAS has elected French tax consolidation or a special regime.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate income tax amount, instalments paid, credits, and balance payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the balance to instalments and withholding credits actually recorded by the French tax administration. Pay any balance through the electronic tax account by the applicable deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Summary of controlled transactions and transfer pricing policy where the statutory turnover or gross-asset threshold and related conditions are met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report cross-border transactions with foreign related parties, including services, loans, royalties, commissions, and cost allocations. Maintain a transaction-level reconciliation to the general ledger and agreements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filed corporate income tax returns generally attract a 10% surcharge, increased in cases of formal notice or abusive conduct and potentially 40% or 80% for serious or fraudulent behavior. Late payment generally bears late-payment interest at 0.20% per month, subject to statutory rules. Failure to use mandatory electronic filing or payment may trigger an additional surcharge, commonly 0.2%, subject to applicable minimums and exceptions. Tax reassessment may also include transfer pricing adjustments, withholding tax, VAT, interest, and fraud-related penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% French withholding tax generally applies to dividends and similar distributions paid by a French company to a non-resident recipient, subject to domestic exemptions and applicable tax treaties. The EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption may apply to a qualifying EU or EEA corporate parent, commonly requiring a qualifying ownership interest, minimum holding conditions, and anti-abuse compliance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of residence from the recipient's foreign tax authority and complete the applicable French treaty forms, commonly Form 5000-FR and the relevant dividend, interest, or royalty annex such as Form 5001-FR. Provide the certified forms to the French payer or withholding agent and retain beneficial-ownership and anti-abuse evidence. If relief is not granted at source, the recipient may generally seek a refund through the applicable French procedure. The French payer must calculate, withhold, report, and remit the tax, generally through Form 2777-SD by the 15th day of the month following the payment month.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and similar payments to non-residents may generally be subject to French withholding tax under Article 182 B of the French Tax Code, commonly at 25%, subject to treaty limitations, EU directive relief, beneficial-ownership requirements, and special rules for non-cooperative jurisdictions. Ordinary interest paid by a French company to a non-resident is generally not subject to French withholding tax, but statutory exceptions apply, including certain payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions and anti-abuse situations. Treaty rates vary by recipient jurisdiction and payment characterization; the applicable treaty must be reviewed before payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 150 million annual pre-tax turnover or gross assets generally triggers the full transfer pricing documentation regime, including Local File and Master File requirements under French law. A simplified transfer pricing declaration may apply at a lower EUR 50 million turnover or gross-assets threshold, or where the taxpayer belongs to a group meeting the statutory threshold. Documentation may also be required below these thresholds where the tax administration requests it or where the transactions are material and controlled.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate a separate regime formally named Economic Substance Regulations equivalent to certain offshore jurisdictions. Substance is nevertheless enforced through the French general anti-abuse rule, abuse-of-law doctrine, beneficial-ownership requirements, controlled foreign company rules, permanent-establishment principles, anti-hybrid rules, interest limitation rules, withholding tax anti-conduit principles, and EU principal-purpose-test concepts. The SAS should maintain real French management, personnel, premises, operational decision-making, books and records, banking, customer-service capacity, and commercial risk consistent with its study-abroad and immigration-consulting activities. A paper intermediary lacking personnel, decision-making, contractual control, or commercial risk may be denied deductions, treaty relief, or beneficial-owner status.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate income tax evasion and fraudulent accounting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing revenue, fabricating expenses, maintaining double books, diverting client deposits, understating taxable profits, or knowingly filing materially false tax returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, 80% fraud surcharge in appropriate cases, late-payment interest, and criminal tax-fraud penalties that may include imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of up to EUR 500,000, with higher penalties in aggravated or organized circumstances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may incur criminal liability, personal tax liability for fraudulent or repeated non-compliance, civil damages, management bans, and asset-seizure measures. Travel restrictions or imprisonment may arise only under applicable judicial or criminal procedures and are not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: VAT fraud and improper treatment of client funds
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to charge or remit French VAT on taxable consultancy services, misclassifying advisory fees as exempt services, issuing false invoices, or using escrow and advance-payment accounts to conceal taxable consideration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT reassessment, interest, penalties generally ranging from 10% to 80% depending on conduct, possible criminal prosecution for fraudulent concealment, and restrictions on business activity in serious cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may be pursued for deliberate or repeated tax non-payment, fraudulent accounting, misuse of corporate assets, or personal guarantees. Criminal imprisonment and fines may apply where the facts constitute tax fraud or related offenses.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length management fees, commissions, royalties, loans, or cost allocations to foreign related parties, or using a foreign affiliate to shift profits from the French SAS without functions, assets, or risks supporting the remuneration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary adjustment, secondary adjustment or constructive distribution treatment, withholding tax, interest, documentation penalties, and a possible 40% or 80% penalty for deliberate or fraudulent conduct. Failure to provide required documentation may attract a statutory penalty linked to the reassessed profits and the statutory minimum.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal liability for deliberate tax evasion, fraudulent management, or knowingly approving unsupported related-party arrangements. The corporate veil is not ordinarily pierced solely because an adjustment is made.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing dividends, interest, or royalties through a conduit entity that lacks beneficial ownership, applying treaty relief without a valid tax residence certificate, or inserting an intermediary principally to obtain a reduced withholding rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty or directive relief, withholding tax reassessment, interest, anti-abuse penalties, and possible 40% or 80% penalties where intent or fraud is established.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve sham or conduit arrangements may face civil restitution, tax-fraud prosecution, management bans, and confiscation measures. Imprisonment is fact-dependent and requires judicial proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed immigration, legal, or regulated advisory activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Representing clients before French authorities without required authorization, providing reserved legal services without being qualified or authorized, arranging fraudulent visa documentation, or guaranteeing immigration outcomes contrary to applicable professional rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative closure, professional sanctions, invalidation of applications, civil damages, criminal prosecution for unauthorized practice, fraud, forgery, or use of forged documents, with fines and imprisonment depending on the offense.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and consultants may be personally liable for client restitution, fraud, forgery, unauthorized practice, and breaches of professional or consumer law. Limited liability does not protect a person from personal criminal conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained third-party wire transfers, failing to identify clients and beneficial owners, not assessing source of funds, ignoring high-risk jurisdictions or politically exposed persons, or failing to report suspicious activity where the business falls within an AML-obligated category.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative sanctions, regulatory reprimands, monetary penalties, suspension or prohibition of activity, confiscation, and criminal penalties for laundering or terrorist-financing participation. Penalties depend on the regulated status and specific offense.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may be personally sanctioned for intentional participation, facilitation, concealment, or serious governance failures. Civil restitution, asset freezing, professional bans, and imprisonment may apply in criminal cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying or offering money, commissions, gifts, or undocumented success fees to public officials, university personnel, visa intermediaries, or agents to obtain admissions, permits, residence documents, or preferential treatment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: French anti-corruption offenses may result in imprisonment and substantial fines, confiscation, exclusion from public procurement, corporate compliance orders, and prosecution of both the company and individuals. Legal entities may face fines up to five times the amount applicable to individuals under relevant criminal provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, employees, and intermediaries may be personally prosecuted for active or passive bribery and influence peddling. Criminal records, asset confiscation, management bans, and imprisonment may result.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Promising guaranteed admission or residence, using fabricated academic or financial documents, concealing refusal risks, misrepresenting government affiliation, or charging undisclosed fees and non-refundable amounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Contract rescission, customer restitution, administrative fines, civil damages, injunctions, and criminal penalties for fraud, forgery, deceptive commercial practices, or misuse of personal data.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals who direct, authorize, or knowingly participate in deceptive or forged-document schemes may be personally liable for restitution and criminal sanctions, including fines and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate asset misuse and unlawful profit extraction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using SAS funds for personal expenses, undocumented shareholder withdrawals, disguised dividends, excessive related-party remuneration, or transfers to a foreign owner unsupported by services or distributions lawfully approved.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate income tax and withholding tax reassessment, denial of deductions, interest, penalties, repayment of improperly distributed assets, and potential abuse of corporate assets prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be ordered to restore corporate assets, compensate creditors, bear insolvency-related liabilities, and face criminal sanctions for misuse of company property or unlawful distributions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Insolvency, creditor prejudice, and late filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Continuing to trade while insolvent, preferring related parties, transferring assets offshore, failing to file for insolvency within the statutory period, or concealing liabilities and tax arrears.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Clawback of transactions, insolvency proceedings, director contribution to insufficient assets, prohibition from managing companies, civil liability, and possible bankruptcy-related criminal penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil restitution, personal contribution to the shortfall, management bans, asset freezes, and imprisonment for fraudulent bankruptcy or asset dissipation. Travel restrictions may be ordered only where legally justified by judicial proceedings.
